headline: Unpacking the 'Knowing-Using Gap': Why LLMs Memorize But Don't Generalize
reasoning: This paper directly addresses a critical, well-known limitation in LLM fine-tuning: the 'Knowing-Using Gap.' Its mechanistic approach to understanding why memorized knowledge fails to generalize, using novel techniques like self-patching, offers significant research value. The proposed diagnostic finding and heuristic strategy to recover generalization headroom are practical and impactful for builders.
summary: New research from arXiv introduces the 'Knowing-Using Gap' to describe why LLMs memorize new facts but struggle to apply them to reasoning tasks. The study uses 'self-patching' to mechanistically understand this failure, attributing it to knowledge-circuit misalignment, and proposes a heuristic strategy to improve generalization.

source_articles.title: Towards Mechanistically Understanding Why Memorized Knowledge Fails to Generalize in Large Language Model Finetuning
source_articles.excerpt: arXiv:2607.08393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Fine-tuning LLMs to inject new knowledge faces a critical challenge: LLMs can quickly memorize new facts, yet fail to use them for downstream reasoning tasks.
